subject.title: fix(gateway): enforce plugin-ownership check in sessions.patch

question: After repairing the head, should plugin-runtime `sessions.patch` fail closed for every legacy ownerless session row, or must upgrades provide a defined operator or doctor recovery path?
rationale: Rejecting ownerless rows strengthens plugin isolation but intentionally stops a previously permitted persisted-state workflow, so automation cannot choose the permanent compatibility and authorization contract.

options.title: Fail closed with recovery
options.body: Keep plugin access denied and add a documented, tested operator or doctor recovery or migration path for legacy ownerless rows.

options.title: Accept strict break
options.body: Keep unconditional ownerless-row rejection and explicitly accept that affected plugin-runtime workflows stop after upgrade.

options.title: Define safe adoption
options.body: Permit ownership adoption only under a narrowly specified and tested authority rule.

recommendation.title: Fail closed with recovery
recommendation.body: Keep plugin access denied and add a documented, tested operator or doctor recovery or migration path for legacy ownerless rows.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent session lifecycle and ownership-adjacent history makes this the strongest available routing candidate for the compatibility and security choice.
